question: What does SKHY's multi-timeframe price structure (1W/1D/4H), institutional volume, and options chain reveal about timing and risk?

epigraph.quote: Never argue with the 50-day moving average when a high-beta leader breaks below it on institutional distribution; let the base rebuild before committing fresh capital.
epigraph.author: Stan Weinstein Stage Analysis Principle

web_blocks.html: On November 13, 2026, SKHY closed at $131.79 (-4.30% on the day), sitting 34.06% below its $199.87 post-IPO high and just 7.85% above its $122.20 52-week low [21, 22]. Because the NASDAQ ADS listed on July 10, 2026, SKHY does not yet have 200 daily bars or 30 weekly bars for a 200D/30W moving average [4, 21, 22]. Nevertheless, every available trend gauge confirms an active Stage 4 markdown (`AVOID_STAGE4_OR_BROKEN`, `CAP_REJECTED`) [22]. Price trades 19.64% below its 50-day SMA ($164.00), 11.96% below its 10-week EMA ($149.69), and 6.77% below its 20-day SMA ($141.36), while the 4-hour chart shows no bullish turn (`intraday_4h_turn = false`, below 4H 20-EMA at $137.48 and 4H 50-SMA at $143.12) [22].

High-beta semiconductor ADRs rarely bottom cleanly until index distribution abates and peer leaders stabilize—yet MU, WDC, STX, TSM, and NVDA are all simultaneously in Stage 4 [22].

web_blocks.title: Institutional Flow, Short Interest & Options Volatility Skew

web_blocks.html: Volume and ownership data reflect an ADR float still undergoing institutional seasoning [21, 22]. On November 13, SKHY traded 16.42M shares, or 0.72x its 30-day average of 22.80M shares—indicating steady selling pressure without a high-volume capitulation washout [22]. Finviz shows U.S. institutional ownership at just 1.55% (up 9.48% quarter-over-quarter) and short interest at 0.50% of float (36.42M shares, 1.75 days to cover) [21]. Meanwhile, across the broader market on November 13, Cboe reported a total put/call ratio of 0.85 and an equity put/call ratio of 0.63—showing hedging demand without extreme panic [27].

web_blocks.title: What a Valid Stage 2 Repair Sequence Would Look Like

web_blocks.html: For SKHY to transition out of Stage 4 and earn fresh capital, three sequential tape milestones must occur [22]. First, price must hold the $119.52–$123.16 support zone and carve a higher low on the 4-hour chart (`intraday_4h_turn = true`) [22]. Second, daily Bollinger Band width must compress from 31.09% toward <15% as volume dries up and sellers exhaust supply [22]. Third, SKHY must reclaim its 50-day SMA ($164.00) on >=1.5x average volume (~34.2M shares/day) while the S&P 500 exits its Correction [22]. Until those three conditions are met, rallies into $141.36–$149.69 remain selling opportunities rather than breakouts [22].

Peer breadth confirms this patience: MU ($778.31 vs. $943.78 50D SMA), WDC ($295.65 vs. $391.72), STX ($528.29 vs. $740.61), TSM ($398.73 vs. $430.11), and NVDA ($162.85 vs. $214.65, RSI 24.86) are all in Stage 4 [22]. When the entire semiconductor complex is below its 50-day averages, individual rebounds routinely stall at the 20-day SMA ($141.36) or 10-week EMA ($149.69) before retesting lows [22].

book_paragraphs: If Chapter 7 showed us that SKHY's 3.25x forward earnings multiple hides a 5.53x price-to-book ratio and a 43.6% U.S. ADR premium, Chapter 8 asks the market's own jury—the price and volume tape—whether institutional buyers are stepping in to defend the stock. On November 13, 2026, the tape's answer is an unambiguous no.

SKHY closed at $131.79, down 4.30% on the session. That leaves the NASDAQ ADR 34.06% below its $199.87 post-IPO peak and just 7.85% above its $122.20 52-week low. Because the ADR only began trading on July 10, 2026, it has not yet accumulated the 200 daily bars or 30 weekly bars required to plot a traditional 200-day simple moving average. Even without that long-term line, however, the multi-timeframe damage across the 4-hour, daily, and weekly charts places SKHY squarely in a Weinstein Stage 4 markdown.

Let us walk down the timeframes systematically. On the weekly chart, SKHY sits 11.96% below its declining 10-week exponential moving average at $149.69, with a weekly RSI of 40.95. On the daily chart, the stock is 19.64% below its 50-day simple moving average at $164.00 and 6.77% below its 20-day simple moving average at $141.36, with a daily RSI of 41.72. Notice that an RSI of 41.72 is weak—confirming bearish momentum—yet not deeply oversold below 30, meaning there is still room for another leg down if support cracks. On the 4-hour intraday chart, price remains pinned below both the 4H 20-EMA ($137.48) and 4H 50-SMA ($143.12), with no reversal turn triggered.

Volatility is also wide and unforgiving. SKHY's 14-day Average True Range is $10.11, or 7.67% of the current share price, and its Bollinger Band width is 31.09%. In a healthy Stage 2 Volatility Contraction Pattern—the kind of tight, quiet base that precedes sustainable breakouts—volatility contracts and price hugs a rising 10-week EMA. Here, the bands are wide open, daily swings routinely exceed 4% to 7%, and the stock carries a 1-year beta of 3.20x. Over the past month, SKHY is down 12.46%, and over the past three months it has fallen 22.16%, even after a brief +2.06% weekly bounce earlier in November that failed to clear resistance.

Macro and sector context reinforce the caution. As of November 13, 2026, the S&P 500 is in an official Correction regime, trading below its 50-day moving average with six institutional distribution days over the past 25 sessions and only 52.6% of index breadth above the 50-day average. Simultaneously, the 10-year U.S. Treasury yield has pushed up to 5.10% against a 4.86% 2-year yield. Across the entire AI memory and semiconductor peer group—Micron, Western Digital, Seagate, TSMC, and NVIDIA—every single peer is in Stage 4 below its 50-day moving average. NVIDIA's daily RSI has even washed out to 24.86, while Western Digital sits at 38.52 and Seagate at 37.06. When the entire complex is liquidating together, trying to catch a falling 3.20-beta ADR in mid-air is a low-probability trade.

book_subsections.title: Institutional Ownership, Volume & The $122.20 Line in the Sand
paragraphs: Examining the volume and ownership plumbing adds further clarity. On November 13, SKHY traded 16.42 million shares, which is only 0.72x its 30-day average volume of 22.80 million shares. There has been no high-volume selling climax or institutional accumulation spike to mark a durable bottom. Meanwhile, Finviz reports U.S. institutional ownership at just 1.55% (up 9.48% quarter-over-quarter) and short interest at 0.50% of float (36.42 million shares, or 1.75 days to cover). Because the U.S. ADR is still new, domestic U.S. mutual funds and pension allocators have barely built core positions, leaving the float vulnerable to fast-money momentum outflows.

This brings us to the critical support and resistance map. Immediately below $131.79 sits the $122.20 52-week low and Pivot S1 at $121.34, defining a technical support zone between $119.52 and $123.16, with a hard structural invalidation stop at $116.28. If $122.20 breaks on heavy volume, there is an air pocket down toward Pivot S2 at $93.48—which, not coincidentally, aligns closely with the ~$91–$95 Seoul KRX ordinary-share parity level! Conversely, any relief bounce faces immediate overhead supply at the 20-day SMA ($141.36) and 10-week EMA ($149.69), followed by Pivot Middle ($158.66) and the 50-day SMA ($164.00).

book_subsections.title: Options Skew & Why Even Cheap Volatility Demands Patience
paragraphs: Interestingly, the options market shows that SKHY's 61-day at-the-money implied volatility of 70.0% sits well below its 20-day realized historical volatility of 101.1%—an IV_CHEAP regime. In theory, cheap implied volatility favors buying defined-risk debit spreads, such as the January 15, 2027 $130/$160 Bull Call Spread priced at $10.31 ($1,031 max loss for $1,969 max profit, a 1.91:1 reward-to-risk ratio with a $140.31 breakeven). Open interest clusters heavily at the $130 strike (21,652 contracts) and $160 strike (3,896 contracts), confirming where institutional dealers have anchored their positioning.

Let us walk through the exact wallet math on that conditional spread so you see both its appeal and its danger. Buying one $130 Call at the $15.93 mid-price and selling one $160 Call at $5.62 costs $10.31 per share, or $1,031.00 total. That $1,031.00 is 103.1 basis points of portfolio NAV and represents your absolute maximum loss. At expiration on January 15, 2027, the spread breaks even at $140.31 (+6.46% above today's close) and hits its maximum $3,000.00 value—a $1,969.00 net profit—anywhere at or above $160.00. Today, net delta adds $29.40 per $1 move up, while net theta costs $2.28 per day.

Yet cheap options do not override a broken Stage 4 chart—nor do they fix a critical calendar mismatch. The January 15, 2027 expiration occurs 12 to 13 days before SK hynix's expected Q4/FY2026 earnings catalyst on January 27–28, 2027, meaning the spread decays to expiration before the fundamental catalyst even arrives. Across the broader market on November 13, Cboe reported a total put/call ratio of 0.85 and an equity put/call ratio of 0.63—showing orderly hedging rather than capitulation. Deploying even a $1,031 debit spread at $131.79 while 4-hour and daily trends point straight down invites daily theta bleed into a falling knife. The disciplined playbook stands aside on options until a Stage 1 base forms and post-earnings March or April 2027 expirations are evaluated.

book_subsections.title: The Three-Step Repair Checklist Before Re-Entry
paragraphs: Technical discipline is not permanent pessimism; it is conditional patience. Before SKHY can earn back a Stage 2 buy rating, we need to see three specific things happen on the tape. First, price must test and hold the $119.52 to $123.16 support shelf and print a confirmed higher low on the 4-hour chart. Second, daily Bollinger Band width must contract from its current 31.09% down below 15% as sellers exhaust themselves and volume dries up. Third, SKHY must break back above its 50-day moving average ($164.00) on at least 1.5x average volume—roughly 34.2 million shares—in a healthy market tape. Until those three boxes are checked, any bounce is guilty until proven innocent.

Let us also connect the tape to the calendar. SK hynix is expected to report Q4 and full-year 2026 results around January 27 to January 28, 2027. That means we are roughly ten weeks away from the next major fundamental catalyst—and explains why a January 15, 2027 option expiration misses the event entirely. In a Stage 4 downtrend during an S&P 500 Correction, stocks rarely go straight up into earnings without first building a proper multi-week base. If SKHY spends November and December testing $122.20 and carving a tight consolidation between $125 and $145, the January earnings report could become the catalyst that launches a true Stage 2 breakout, at which point post-earnings March or April 2027 expirations can be evaluated cleanly.

Conversely, if the broader market suffers another wave of institutional distribution and SKHY closes below $121.34 on heavy volume, waiting for a bounce would be a mistake. Respecting the $121.34 Pivot S1 level and the $116.28 invalidation stop ensures that a cyclical correction never turns into a permanent capital impairment.

Let us also put the 1-year beta of 3.20x into plain dollar terms for a portfolio manager. When the S&P 500 drops 1% during a Correction session, a 3.20-beta stock historically moves more than 3% in the same direction. On November 13, 2026, SKHY fell 4.30% on a single day, wiping out nearly two weeks of modest stabilization. With an Average True Range of $10.11 per day, normal daily noise can swing a $2,341 position by nearly $180 in a single afternoon.

That is why Stan Weinstein's stage rules are so unforgiving about Stage 4 stocks. Once price breaks below the 50-day moving average ($164.00) and the 10-week EMA ($149.69), every prior buyer between $150 and $199 sits underwater and looks for rallies to sell into. Until that overhead supply is absorbed through time and tight consolidation, the path of least resistance remains sideways to down.

To make this concrete, trace the supply shelves above $131.79. First, short-term traders who bought the early-November bounce will look to exit near the 20-day SMA at $141.36 and the 4-hour 50-SMA at $143.12. Second, swing buyers from October sit trapped near the 10-week EMA at $149.69. Third, institutional buyers from September and August sit underwater between Pivot Middle at $158.66 and the 50-day SMA at $164.00. Clearing three separate layers of trapped supply requires sustained institutional accumulation, not a one-day dead-cat bounce.

In addition, watch the broader semiconductor ETF and peer leadership. When NVIDIA sits at a 24.86 daily RSI and Micron trades 17.5% below its own 50-day moving average, active fund managers are reducing gross semiconductor exposure across the board rather than rotating into high-beta Korean ADRs. Until sector-wide distribution ends, patience remains the highest-return trade.
